high.title: First Bank to Announce Savings Interest Rate Increase Since the Start of July
high.summary:
Bac A Bank (North Asia Commercial Joint Stock Bank) has become the first Vietnamese commercial bank to raise its listed deposit interest rates in July 2026. The bank implemented a uniform rate schedule for individual customers, eliminating its previous tiered structure that differentiated between deposits below and above VND 1 billion — effectively granting smaller depositors access to previously higher-tier rates.

Key rate changes: Short-term deposits (1–5 months) now yield **4.75% p.a.**; medium-term deposits (6–11 months) moved to **7.05% p.a.**; the 12-month rate — the key benchmark — rose to **7.10% p.a.** (+20 bps); and 13–36 month tenors were adjusted to **6.95% p.a.**

high.title: Maybank Analysis Director Identifies Key Factor Determining Future Interest Rate Trends
high.summary:
Maybank Vietnam's Head of Securities Analysis, Quan Trong Thanh, offers a nuanced view on Vietnam's banking system liquidity and interest rate outlook. He argues that the current Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) of 112–115% — driven by a gap of approximately VND 2.6 quadrillion between credit growth and deposit mobilization as of Q1/2026 — is not abnormal when viewed in full context. Crucially, he identifies **inflation, not liquidity tightness per se, as the primary upward pressure on interest rates**. This is a meaningful distinction for bond investors: if inflation data for July and August 2026 continues the positive trend seen in June, interest rates could begin to ease from around **September 2026**. For VND bond traders, this is a key signal — a September rate inflection point would support duration extension strategies in government bonds. FX implications are also notable: easing rates could put mild downward pressure on VND if rate differentials with USD compress. Watch July and August CPI prints as the critical trigger for SBV's next policy move.

---

high.title: Savings Interest Rates Reach 9% Per Annum — Depositors Rushing to Switch Banks at Maturity
high.summary: Deposit rates in Vietnam have climbed to as high as 9% per annum, with meaningful dispersion across institutions — some banks still offering 8% while competitors post 8.8%+, prompting retail depositors to actively switch banks at maturity rather than auto-renew. The article highlights that certificate of deposit (CD) products are also attracting strong demand as savers seek to lock in peak yields. MBS Securities' latest research note signals that the upward momentum in deposit funding costs may be showing early signs of plateauing, though rates remain elevated.

medium.title: VN-Index Plunges Nearly 50 Points Before Recovering — What Should Equity Investors Do?
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market opened the new week on July 13 with sharp volatility — the VN-Index at one point shed nearly 48 points before buyers emerged at lower levels, trimming the close to a loss of approximately 28 points. The index managed to hold the psychologically important 1,800-point level. Breadth was heavily negative, with 271 stocks declining versus only 52 advancing on HoSE, and 27 of 30 VN30 blue-chip stocks closing in the red. Trading value on HoSE was modest at approximately VND 17,900 billion, suggesting cautious sentiment with buyers unwilling to commit aggressively despite the intraday price dip. A partial recovery was attributed to select banking stocks absorbing selling pressure. For fund managers, the inability to sustain buying momentum and weak liquidity amid a significant intraday drawdown signals continued market fragility. The 1,800-point level remains a critical support zone to monitor.

medium.title: Gold Enters a "Pivotal Week" — Experts Highlight Key Factors to Watch Closely
medium.summary: Gold markets pulled back last week as the USD and US Treasury yields rose simultaneously, with spot gold closing around **$4,120/oz** (down 1.32% week-on-week) and COMEX August futures at $4,128/oz — now down nearly 6% year-to-date. The Fed's June meeting minutes revealed some officials remain open to further rate hikes given persistent inflation concerns, dampening gold's safe-haven appeal. Domestically, SJC gold closed the week at approximately VND 146.9 million/tael (buy) and VND 149.9 million/tael (sell), down roughly 1% week-on-week. While gold is not a direct VND/USD instrument, the USD strength narrative and Fed hawkishness have direct implications for VND exchange rate pressure and SBV's reserve management posture. Investors should monitor upcoming US economic data releases this week as potential catalysts for both gold and USD direction.

medium.title: Surprising Latest NPL Trends at Vietcombank, Agribank, Sacombank, ABBank...
medium.summary:
As of 30 June 2026, non-performing loan (NPL) ratios across Vietnam's banking system are broadly stable or improving, with notable exceptions. Vietcombank maintains one of the system's lowest NPL ratios at below 1% (Q1 2026: 0.62%), while Agribank holds steady at 1.13%. ABBank reported the sharpest improvement, with NPL expected to fall to approximately 0.55% from 0.85% at end-Q1 2026. The outlier is Sacombank, where CEO Loic Faussier disclosed that the NPL ratio could surge to approximately 5.6% (vs. 5.01% at end-Q1 2026), driven by legacy ownership-related restructuring issues, NIM compression, and potentially record-high provisioning costs in the period ahead.

**Relevance:** Banking sector asset quality is a key macro signal for Vietnam's credit cycle. Sacombank's deteriorating NPL trajectory warrants monitoring — elevated provisioning costs will weigh on earnings and could reduce the bank's capacity to absorb government bonds. Broader system stability at Vietcombank and Agribank (the two largest state-owned commercial banks) provides a cushion. This data is relevant for both banking equity positions and assessing systemic credit risk that could influence SBV policy decisions.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Ring Gold Prices on July 13: Drop by Up to VND 2.2 Million per Tael
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell sharply on the afternoon of July 13, with SJC gold bars declining VND 1.5 million per tael to VND 145.4–148.4 million per tael. Ring gold products saw even steeper corrections of up to VND 2.2 million per tael across major dealers including SJC, DOJI, Bảo Tín Minh Châu, and Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải. The broad-based decline across all major gold retailers suggests this is driven by global gold price movements rather than domestic supply factors. While gold is not a direct FX instrument in Vietnam, sharp gold price moves are monitored by the SBV as they can influence USD/VND dynamics — periods of rising gold prices historically correlate with increased USD demand for gold imports, adding pressure to the VND. The current pullback in gold prices is therefore marginally VND-supportive.

medium.title: Stock Investors: What Should They Do After VN-Index Plunged Nearly 50 Points Before Recovering?
medium.summary: Vietnam's equity market opened the week on a highly volatile note in the July 13 session, with the VN-Index at one point falling nearly 48 points before recovering to close down approximately 28 points, holding the psychologically important 1,800-point level. On HoSE, declining stocks overwhelmingly outnumbered advancers (271 vs. 52), with 27 of 30 stocks in the VN30 basket closing lower, indicating concentrated selling pressure in large-cap names. Trading liquidity was modest at approximately VND 17,900 billion matched on HoSE, suggesting buyers remain cautious despite intraday price dips. The partial recovery was attributed to selective buying in banking stocks. For fund managers, the resilience at 1,800 points is a key technical level to monitor; a sustained break below could trigger further capital outflows and weigh on broader market sentiment.

medium.title: US and Iran Both Claim Control of the Strait of Hormuz — Middle East Tensions Escalate
medium.summary: Tensions in the Middle East sharply escalated after Iran attacked a container vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on July 12. Both the US and Iran are claiming jurisdictional authority over the waterway, with Iran asserting the right to regulate and charge transit fees under a temporary agreement reached last month — a position firmly rejected by Washington, which is now seeking alternative shipping routes outside Iranian control. The two sides are roughly halfway through a 60-day negotiation window aimed at a permanent ceasefire and nuclear deal, but the renewed attacks risk derailing talks. UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned on July 13 that a return to large-scale conflict would have "catastrophic consequences." Oil prices surged nearly 5% on July 13 before partially retracing. **Relevance for Vietnam:** As a major oil importer and export-dependent economy, sustained oil price spikes add upward pressure on Vietnam's inflation and trade costs, which could weigh on VND stability and complicate SBV's room to ease monetary policy. Elevated global risk aversion could also trigger foreign equity outflows from frontier/EM markets including Vietnam. Watch oil price trajectory and VN-Index foreign net flows closely.

medium.title: Two Trillion-Dollar Giants Sold Over 100 Tonnes of Gold in Just a Few Months
medium.summary: State Street Global Advisors (SSGA) and BlackRock — managers of the world's largest gold ETFs — have been net sellers of gold since their holdings peaked in February 2026. SSGA's SPDR Gold Trust family (GLD, GLDM) has offloaded approximately 88 tonnes, while BlackRock's iShares gold products (IAU, SGLN, IAUM) have reduced holdings by roughly 25 tonnes — a combined net sale of ~113 tonnes in a matter of months. The article notes this does not necessarily signal institutional abandonment of gold, but does reflect a shift in positioning. **Relevance for Vietnam:** Large institutional gold selling globally tends to reduce gold prices, which can ease pressure on Vietnam's domestic gold market — a key driver of unofficial USD demand and VND volatility. If global gold prices soften, the SBV may face reduced speculative pressure on the VND-gold-USD arbitrage dynamic. Worth monitoring in conjunction with domestic gold pricing spreads.

medium.title: Investors' Woes: Nearly 900 Stocks in Decline, Portfolios Down Tens of Percent
medium.summary: The VN-Index continues to struggle around the 1,800-point level, broadly flat year-to-date. However, the headline index masks significant underlying weakness in market breadth. Of the more than 1,500 listed stocks across all three exchanges, 888 have posted negative returns since the start of the year, with over 200 names down more than 20%. Notable losers include FPT, SSI, VRE, DXG, and SHS. Retail investors report mid-cap portfolio drawdowns of 15–30%, even where fundamentals appear sound. This divergence between index stability and broad market deterioration is a key signal for equity investors: the 1,800 level is being supported by a narrow set of large-cap names, while liquidity and sentiment remain fragile beneath the surface. For fund managers, this environment suggests elevated stock-specific risk, potential forced selling from leveraged retail accounts, and limited near-term upside catalyst unless macro conditions — including SBV policy or USD/VND stability — improve materially.

medium.title: Prosecution of Multiple Business Owners and Gold Shop Operators in Transnational Diamond Smuggling Ring
medium.summary: On July 12, 2026, the Criminal Investigation Agency of Thanh Hoa Province initiated prosecution of four additional suspects — including directors of gold and gemstone trading companies in Ho Chi Minh City — on charges of smuggling under Article 188 of the Penal Code. The suspects allegedly used social media applications to coordinate cross-border diamond transactions. Notably, one suspect is an employee of PNJ's appraisal subsidiary (PNJ-LAP), raising potential reputational and regulatory concerns for one of Vietnam's largest listed jewelry and gold retailers. For market participants, enforcement actions targeting the informal gold and precious metals trade are worth monitoring as they can reflect broader SBV concerns about unregulated capital flows and foreign currency/gold hoarding outside official channels — dynamics that have historically influenced VND liquidity conditions.

medium.title: Over VND 9.4 Quadrillion in Customer Deposits Flowed into 27 Banks Over the Past 10 Years: Which Bank Attracted the Most?
medium.summary:
Total customer deposits across 27 listed Vietnamese banks surged from approximately VND 3.4 quadrillion at end-2015 to over VND 12.8 quadrillion by end-2025 — a near 4x increase over the decade, adding roughly VND 940 trillion per year on average. This structural deepening of the deposit base reflects robust economic expansion, rising household incomes, growing corporate balance sheets, and accelerating digital banking adoption. For bond and FX market participants, this trend is a key indicator of system-wide liquidity conditions and the banking sector's capacity to absorb government bond issuance. A deeper, more stable deposit base reduces banks' reliance on interbank funding and supports their role as primary dealers in the government bond market. It also signals ongoing confidence in the VND as a store of value — a constructive backdrop for the domestic currency. Investors should monitor whether deposit growth momentum continues into H2 2026, particularly in the context of any SBV rate adjustments or shifting risk appetite toward equities and gold.

---

medium.title: Foreign Capital Race to Acquire Vietnamese Pharmaceutical Companies Intensifies — A $10 Billion Market at Stake
medium.summary: Vietnam's pharmaceutical sector — projected to reach $10 billion in market value — is attracting accelerating M&A activity from both international pharmaceutical conglomerates and domestic financial groups. According to SHS Research, the 2025–2030 period marks a new growth cycle for the sector, transitioning from generic drug manufacturing toward modern production ecosystems meeting international standards. The wave of inbound foreign direct investment (FDI) through M&A transactions is broadly relevant to Vietnam's capital flow dynamics. While not a direct FX or rates story, sustained foreign strategic investment in domestic industries supports Vietnam's current account and provides a partial offset to portfolio outflow pressures currently evident in equities. Fund managers should monitor whether FDI-linked M&A flows are being captured in SBV reserve accumulation data in coming months.

medium.title: A Turbulent Week for Gold and Silver Prices
medium.summary:
Gold and silver markets — both domestically in Vietnam and globally — experienced broad-based declines during the trading week of July 6–12, 2026. The primary drivers were a recovery in the USD, the Federal Reserve's sustained hawkish posture, and escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Domestic SJC gold bars closed the week at VND 146.9 million/tael (buy) and VND 149.9 million/tael (sell), with prices extending their slide into the opening session of July 13, trading in the VND 145–148.4 million/tael range — representing a decline of approximately 1.6% over seven days. For VND and Vietnamese asset traders, a strengthening USD and a risk-off global environment are key watchpoints: USD strength typically exerts depreciation pressure on the VND, which could prompt SBV intervention or FX reserve adjustments. Additionally, softening gold prices domestically may reduce speculative demand for gold — a traditional store of value in Vietnam — potentially influencing retail savings behavior and deposit flows into the banking system. Watch the Fed's next communications and Middle East developments for directional cues.

---
